title: Last Day Co: Small Business Wind-Down
one_liner: A flat-fee retirement service for owners who do not want to sell, just stop: legal wind-down, lease exit, records custody, customer-list handoff and a proper last day.
customer: Retiring owners of solo and micro businesses with $100k to $2M in revenue. Start with regulated solo practices (therapists, small medical or dental practices, solo attorneys, CPAs) where closing duties create urgency, then salons, restaurants and contractors.
problem: McKinsey estimates baby boomers run as many as 6M small and midsize US businesses, with roughly 2.3M to 3M expected to transition ownership this decade, yet only about 54% of owners have a succession plan and about a third of owners over 50 say they cannot find a buyer. Brokers are paid only on sales and skip tiny firms, so most simply shut. That leaves leases, personal guarantees, client records, final payroll and taxes, licenses and customers stranded.
solution: A productized 90-day closure: state and local filings and final taxes through a partner CPA, lease exit negotiation (buyout or assignment, limiting the personal guarantee), equipment and inventory liquidation, and a records-custody service where Last Day Co acts as professional custodian for 7 to 10 years with client notice and a release process. It also brokers the customer list or goodwill to a vetted local competitor, with a fee to the owner. It closes with a last-day package: customer letter, farewell event, staff reference packets.
why_now: Boomers are now roughly 62 to 80, so closures are rising toward the McKinsey-projected peak. LLMs make state-specific closure checklists, notices and letters cheap to produce accurately. Remote records custody removes the need for a physical archive.
revenue_model: A $2,500 to $9,000 flat wind-down fee. Records custody at $25 to $75 per month or a prepaid $1,500 for 7 years. A goodwill-handoff success fee of 10% to 20% of what the acquirer pays. A 10% to 15% liquidation commission.
non_obvious_insight: Brokers sell, and nobody closes. Most owners do not want a sale process, they want to stop, so the real product is permission and completion with liability handled. Custodianship for regulated practices is near-zero-churn recurring revenue, and the customer list is the only asset that survives a closure, so a warm handoff to a neighboring competitor is where the money is.
first_30_days: Pick solo therapists and solo attorneys in one state. With a local attorney and CPA, write the state-specific 'professional will and closure' playbook. Sell the $299 professional will plus closure plan through the state association newsletter and LinkedIn. Do three discounted pilot closures end to end, build a list of local acquirers for goodwill handoffs, and document each step as a repeatable checklist.

title: ZIP-Level Appetite Radar for Distressed Markets
one_liner: A live map of which carriers are actually binding homes in which distressed ZIPs, sold to agents and to carriers owing coverage quotas.
customer: Independent agents and wholesale brokers in California (then Florida and Colorado). Carriers pay for pre-qualified submissions in ZIPs where they owe quota.
problem: The CA FAIR Plan hit 696,562 policies (up 8% since Sept 2025) and raised rates about 29.1%. Under the Sustainable Insurance Strategy, carriers get rate freedom in exchange for an 85% writing commitment in distressed ZIPs. Zurich, Mercury and CSAA say they are expanding, yet the June 2026 regulator release gave no numbers. Agents burn hours on declines, and nobody can see the ZIP-by-ZIP flip.
solution: Combine agent-contributed anonymized quote outcomes, licensed quote probing and rate/rule filing monitoring. Publish which carriers bind in each ZIP by roof age and mitigation class, with estimated savings versus FAIR. Agents get a 'who will write this' answer in seconds. Carriers pay a bounty per bound policy.
why_now: California's rewritten rulebook took effect in 2026 while regulator disclosure stayed opaque, so the information gap is largest now.
revenue_model: $99-249/month per agent, plus $75-200 carrier bounties per bound policy.
non_obvious_insight: Headlines say California is broken, but reality is a patchwork flipping ZIP by ZIP. Carriers with quota obligations are price-insensitive buyers of distribution, and agents are blind to them.
first_30_days: Recruit 20 independent agencies in wildfire-adjacent counties to a shared outcome log (a form and spreadsheet is enough). Publish a weekly 'who is writing' report and start charging at week four.

title: AI Standardized Clients for Counseling Programs
one_liner: Voice-based AI 'clients' with persistent backstories, scored on accredited-skills rubrics, give master's students hundreds of rehearsal sessions before real practicum.
customer: Counseling, social-work and MFT master's programs (CACREP-accredited and similar), then OT and PT programs for patient-interview training; the department or a student lab fee pays.
problem: Practicum placements and faculty supervision are scarce. Human standardized clients cost about $30-60 an hour, and classmate role-plays are low fidelity. The new loan caps squeeze programs in excluded fields, and students need repetitions in high-stakes skills like suicide-risk assessment and motivational interviewing.
solution: Real-time voice client agents that stay consistent across sessions, remember last week, vary in difficulty and present safety-critical scenarios. Sessions are auto-scored on rubrics (reflective listening, risk questions asked, missed cues), supervisors review flagged clips, and sessions are logged as pre-practicum skills hours. Rehearsal volume is multiplied, not supervised hours replaced.
why_now: Low-latency, natural voice models with long-term memory reached usable fidelity in 2025-26. Programs in excluded fields face cost pressure after July 2026, and therapist demand remains strong.
revenue_model: $75-200 per student per semester as a lab fee, or $15-40k site licenses per program.
non_obvious_insight: What was infeasible was a client who stays consistent over sessions and reacts with emotion in real time. The binding constraint in clinical training is rehearsal volume, which is exactly what AI supplies cheaply, without threatening the human-supervised hours that licensure requires.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 counseling programs through adjunct faculty who teach skills labs. Build 6 scenarios (intake, motivational interviewing, suicide risk) and run a spring pilot. Measure improvement on the program's existing skills rubric and price at about $100 per student. Build in clinical safety review and privacy controls.

title: Recycled-Content Claim Defense Files
one_liner: Litigation-grade, SKU-level substantiation files for recycled-content claims, built on purchase-to-claim reconciliation rather than more certificates.
customer: General counsel and heads of sustainability at mid-market consumer brands ($100M-$2B revenue) with 'recycled' claims on pack, and retailer private-label teams.
problem: California vetoed AB 2253 (recycled-content claim substantiation) citing 'economic headwinds.' State PCR mandates are slipping (NJ to 2029). Mass-balance accounting is contested and no standard exists. Brands keep making claims for retailers and consumers, while the burden of proving them lands on legal departments via plaintiffs, AGs and retailer audits.
solution: A SKU-level claim file: verify supplier certificates, reconcile volume of certified resin bought against recycled-content claims across all SKUs, and produce a plain-language legal memo on which claims are safe. Add an annual refresh with change alerts. Partner with an insurer for defense-cost coverage credits.
why_now: The veto removed the one route to a state safe harbor and the mandate delays weaken the compliance pretext, so brands are exposed to claim risk without clear rules. Two years of contested mass-balance debate leave no accepted method.
revenue_model: $3-8K per SKU family for the initial file, $20-60K per year retainer, and referral fees from insurers and law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody is short of certificates. Brands are short of reconciliation: a certificate proves a supplier's volume, not that a brand's claims across 400 SKUs are arithmetically supportable.
first_30_days: Build a spreadsheet reconciliation template. Partner with one litigation-defense law firm. Scrape retail listings for '% recycled' claims to find targets. Sell 5 paid claim audits at about $5K each.

title: Unfreeze Desk for Indian UPI Merchants
one_liner: A court-ready dossier generator and fixed-fee advocate network that unfreezes shopkeepers' bank accounts after a scam victim's UPI money passes through them, with a freeze-continuity layer later.
customer: Small merchants, traders, fuel-station owners and freelancers in India whose current or savings accounts get frozen because a scam victim's money passed through their UPI QR. They pay per case (₹3,000-8,000) or a ₹199/month subscription. Chartered accountants and trader associations are the referral channel.
problem: Automated cyber-fraud freezes catch innocent recipients. One Faridabad scam of ₹4.43 crore led to more than 36,000 frozen accounts, mostly small merchants. A Mumbai shop owner was frozen over ₹826 and spent over a month trying to get access back. A retailer's ₹8.26 lakh current account was blocked over a single ₹1,000 UPI payment. Relief takes months, and working capital, payroll and supplier payments stall.
solution: Merchants upload the bank statement and freeze notice, and software extracts the flagged credit, payer VPA, invoices and merchant-vintage evidence. It then produces a bundle for the bank nodal officer and police investigating officer, and a draft writ petition citing the Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Rajasthan High Court rulings that a merchant cannot verify each UPI payer. Partner advocates file and appear at a fixed fee, and the tool tracks the case. Phase 2: a 'clean receipts' setup (order-ID dynamic QR, invoice per payment, a separate working-capital account) and an NBFC-funded bridge advance against the frozen balance.
why_now: The Andhra Pradesh High Court ruled in July 2026 that authorities cannot freeze a merchant's whole account for receiving a UPI payment from an accused, and other High Courts have said the same. That gives a template-able legal remedy where before it was ad hoc. The Faridabad freezes and the Home Ministry review put the problem in the news. UPI acceptance among tiny merchants keeps growing.
revenue_model: Fixed case fee of ₹3,000-8,000 (unfreeze package plus advocate), a ₹199/month 'Merchant Shield' subscription that keeps an evidence dossier updated, and referral fees from NBFC partners for frozen-balance bridge loans. Later B2B licensing to UPI QR aggregators and bank merchant-onboarding teams.
non_obvious_insight: The merchant is not defrauded. The loss is working capital held hostage by a blunt automated tool that recovers almost nothing, so banks over-freeze. A Parliamentary Standing Committee found only ₹0.57 crore recovered out of ₹2,294.79 crore lost to cyber fraud in 2022, about 0.02%. So the freeze is structural false-positive management, not an anti-fraud problem, and the buyer is desperate on day one. Police in Faridabad said 'People come crying. Some had only ₹200 or ₹500 transferred to their accounts, yet the banks froze them.' Evidence: https://the420.in/faridabad-cyber-scam-upi-fraud-accounts-frozen-home-ministry/ and https://www.medianama.com/2026/07/223-merchants-bank-accounts-frozen-upi-payments-fraudsters-andhra-hc/.
first_30_days: Days 1-5: Build a WhatsApp intake bot and landing page in Hindi and English ('Account freeze ho gaya? 10 minute mein case file'). Sign 3 partner advocates in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Hyderabad at a fixed split. Days 5-15: Template the dossier and petition from the three High Court rulings and have the advocates review it. Post explainer videos in Hindi and Gujarati on YouTube and Reels, and in trader WhatsApp and Telegram groups where frozen merchants already vent. Days 15-30: Close the first 20-30 paid cases, publish anonymized turnaround times, and approach two CA firms and one trader association for referrals. The design must keep filings with licensed advocates to avoid unauthorized-practice issues.

title: PTO Bureau: Cash Advances Priced on Utility Delay
one_liner: A data co-op plus bridge lender that advances the 10-20% held back until utility Permission-to-Operate, and prices each advance from real per-utility delay history.
customer: Small and mid-size residential installers doing about 50-500 systems a year ($2-15M revenue). Their cash is squeezed post-25D. Secondary buyers are TPO sponsors and developers who need systems energized before the Dec 31, 2027 placed-in-service cliff.
problem: Lenders and TPO sponsors release most of the money at install but hold back the final 10-20% until PTO. Installer-reported PTO waits run 4-12 weeks, and about 8-12 weeks for battery systems in SCE territory. That holdback is often the entire gross margin, so an installer with 60-100 unenergized systems is one supplier-credit squeeze from insolvency. For TPO systems that did not begin construction by July 4, 2026, the 30% 48E credit requires placed-in-service by Dec 31, 2027, and tax-equity investors generally treat PTO as that trigger. Every idle week is now worth real money to sponsors.
solution: Three pieces. (1) A PTO clock: a member-contributed dataset of submit-to-PTO days by utility, AHJ, system size, and whether it includes storage, plus the recurring deficiency-notice reasons. (2) Bridge advances: buy or advance against the PTO holdback within 48 hours of a passed final inspection, priced from the clock, for example 3-6% for a system expected under 60 days. (3) PTO SWAT: a human team with utility-portal expertise that fixes and re-submits deficient interconnection packages, sold per system, and sold to sponsors as a deadline bounty for clearing backlog before the 2027 cutoff.
why_now: 25D expired Dec 31, 2025 and TPO is now the main route to a federal credit. The 48E begin-construction window closed July 4, 2026, so the 12/31/2027 placed-in-service deadline is now the binding constraint. Storm and battery-heavy interconnection queues are growing, and NEC 2026 adoption is adding deficiency notices. Traditional lenders are pulling back from small installers after the 2025-26 failures.
revenue_model: Discount fee on advances, roughly 25-40% annualized. A $150-300 per-system SWAT fee. Sponsor-paid bounties for pre-deadline energization. A later license of the PTO clock dataset to lenders, tax-equity investors and utilities.
non_obvious_insight: PTO delay looks random to outsiders but is predictable, because it comes from a few utility reviewer queues and about ten repeat deficiency reasons: single-line diagram mismatches, label errors, battery configuration and inverter list issues. Installers know their own utility's clock, but nobody has pooled it. A tiny lender that underwrites on predicted PTO days can beat big finance companies. The collateral is also better than it looks, because the system is already built and has passed the local inspection.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 installers in a single utility territory. Trade a free benchmark report for their last 12 months of PTO timestamps. Publish the resulting utility PTO clock as a lead magnet. Line up a $250-500k line from a community lender or family office. Fund the first 20 advances at installers that sell directly to a sponsor, where assignment consent is easiest. Run the SWAT service as a manual concierge for $200 per system to learn the deficiency patterns.

title: Court-Safe Esper Machine From Bystander Video
one_liner: Blade Runner's Esper machine, made honest: a scaled, non-generative 3D reconstruction of an accident scene from mixed dashcam, doorbell, CCTV and phone clips, with error bars built to survive an admissibility challenge.
customer: Personal-injury law firms, insurer subrogation and special-investigation units, defense counsel and municipal risk managers, initially in disputed-liability vehicle and pedestrian cases with three or more video clips.
problem: Cases turn on several shaky clips. Traditional reconstruction by an expert costs thousands of dollars and takes weeks. Generative 'enhancement' gets challenged or excluded because AI invents pixels, and Gaussian-splat models look convincing but have no verified real-world scale.
solution: Ingest all clips, time-sync them (audio fingerprints, sirens, shared events), solve camera poses, and recover metric scale automatically from regulated-size objects in frame: lane-stripe cycles, stop and speed signs, crosswalk widths, license plates and standard curb heights. Output a measurable model with per-measurement error bars and a 'no generated pixels' guarantee (every pixel traceable to a source frame), plus vehicle speed and trajectory estimates and sightline views ('could the driver see the pedestrian?'). A partner licensed reconstructionist signs the report and serves as expert of record.
why_now: Feed-forward multi-view reconstruction and Gaussian splatting made casual-video reconstruction cheap in the last two years. Courts and defense bars are actively litigating AI-enhanced video. Doorbell, dashcam and storefront cameras mean most incidents now have several angles.
revenue_model: $900-2,500 per case, a discount tier for firms on subscription, and an expert-testimony fee split with the reconstructionist.
non_obvious_insight: Admissibility, not photorealism, is the product. Lawyers would rather have an ugly model with error bars than a beautiful hallucination, and automatic metric scale from objects whose dimensions are set by traffic-control standards is the unlock that separates this from generic splat tools and from drone-only videogrammetry.
first_30_days: Recruit one reconstructionist as expert of record. Offer 10 PI firms a free second-opinion reconstruction on live cases with at least three clips, then charge $1,200 for the next. Target five paying cases by day 90 and a written methods statement reviewed by a litigator.

title: Size Ladder: Circular Wardrobes for GLP-1 Users
one_liner: A subscription that ships the next clothing size on the GLP-1 titration schedule, takes back the last, stores a 'restart' wardrobe, and routes the excess into resale and recycling, sold through telehealth partners as a retention perk.
customer: Cash-pay GLP-1 patients ($59-129 a month), telehealth and clinic operators paying a per-member fee for retention, and plus-size apparel brands and textile-EPR schemes that need diverted volume.
problem: Users move through three to five sizes in 12-18 months, and only about a third are still on therapy at one year while roughly 60% of ex-users plan to restart and stoppers regain about two thirds within a year. So closets fill with clothes that fit neither the current body nor the likely future one. The US textile recycling rate is 14.7% and California alone landfills 1.2M tons a year. Telehealth players have converged on the same $149-$349 price, so they need non-price loyalty features.
solution: At each dose step or every 10 lb, ship the next size from a pooled inventory of pre-owned and new pieces, take back the previous size, and offer take-in tailoring as an alternative. A 'restart wardrobe' bank holds the prior size for 12 months for a small fee. With consent, the telehealth partner shares titration stage so the platform can forecast sizes; in return the clinician sees a behavioral signal when size changes stall or reverse.
why_now: Cash-pay pills at $149 have widened the user base (22% of households have a user) and moved buying away from insurers to consumers who are already spending more on skincare and fragrance. California's textile EPR (SB 707) is moving toward fee-setting, creating a funded outlet for take-back volume. Compounding's exit has pushed users onto branded cash-pay channels that want stickiness.
revenue_model: Consumer subscription, partner PMPM fees ($3-6) from telehealth for retention, brand sponsorship from apparel companies, and resale margin plus EPR diversion credits on the outflow.
non_obvious_insight: Titration is a clock. Because dose steps predict weight-loss milestones, the apparel demand curve is forecastable in a way no fashion category ever is, and the closet is the earliest behavioral read-out of regain.
first_30_days: Recruit 50 patients from GLP-1 patient communities and one partner clinic. Source pre-owned plus-size inventory cheaply from thrift and textile sorters. Line up a tailor network. Run a 3-month pilot at $79 a month, tracking return rates, size churn and how well titration stage predicts the next size.

title: Organized Play in a Box for New Card Games
one_liner: A managed service that gives new and crowdfunded trading card games tournament software, judge training, local-game-store onboarding and prize logistics.
customer: New TCG publishers with funded campaigns (for example the Cyberpunk TCG, which raised $28.35M on Kickstarter in April 2026), and their distributors.
problem: Pokemon has sold 85B+ cards, and new TCGs live or die by weekly events at local game stores. First-time creators have big print-run budgets but no rules-aware tournament engine, judge program, store network or prize support. Kickstarter success does not equal retention.
solution: Rules-aware tournament software (decklist validation, banlist updates, Swiss pairing), a certified judge program, store onboarding kits (demo decks, promos, shipping), an event calendar and reporting, and results-integrity tooling.
why_now: The TCG boom and $28M crowdfunding raises create a wave of well-funded first-time publishers. Stores will only stock games with events.
revenue_model: $5-25k per month retainer per game plus $10-30 per event and margin on store kits.
non_obvious_insight: Kickstarter funds the print run, but retention is in weekly events, and store owners only back games that have them. The infrastructure is game-agnostic, so it amortizes across many small TCGs.
first_30_days: Pitch 20 creators of funded TCG campaigns above $250k. Run a pilot kit at 20 stores. Assemble an open-source tournament engine and sell the first two retainers.

title: Off-Ramp Cohorts for AI-Companion Dependence
one_liner: Eight-week, in-person, non-shaming cohorts that help heavy AI-companion users rebuild human contact, sold to individuals and to employee assistance and counseling providers.
customer: Adults roughly 22-45 who spend two or more hours a day with AI companions (Replika, Character.AI, voice-mode chatbots), plus their worried partners and parents. Second wave: EAP vendors, university counseling centers and behavioral-health plans that have no protocol for this.
problem: Research suggests companions relieve loneliness in small doses but deepen it with heavy daily use; a two-year Aalto study of nearly 2,000 Replika users reportedly found heavy use raised the perceived cost of human relationships and tracked with more depression and loneliness. Lawsuits (Character.AI and Google settled the Garcia case in January 2026) and new laws (California SB 243 in effect since January 1, 2026, Washington HB 2225 signed in March) put the harm on the record, but clinicians have no playbook, users feel judged, and therapy waitlists are long.
solution: A harm-reduction curriculum, not abstinence. Week by week, participants audit what the companion provides (constant availability, validation, safe rehearsal), then re-home each need with a human equivalent: a weekly cohort dinner, a scheduled 'warm call' partner, rehearsal of hard conversations with a facilitator, and a graduated time-box on usage. Ten people per city per cohort, led by trained coaches with a licensed clinician supervising, screening for crisis, and referring out when needed. Pre/post measurement with a validated loneliness scale. Ends with a graduation dinner rather than a discharge.
why_now: Companion apps now have tens of millions of users, the APA flagged AI relationships as a major 2026 trend, and settlements and state laws have made 'what happens to heavy users' a public question. Operators under companion-chatbot laws need credible places to send users, and no incumbent exists. The EU AI Act provisions covering companion-style products are phasing in through 2026.
revenue_model: $395 per seat for an 8-week consumer cohort; $150-250 per seat through EAP and counseling partners; $1,200 curriculum license plus about $30 per participant for therapists and coaches who run their own cohorts; later, outcomes-based contracts with behavioral-health plans.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody pays to 'quit', but people pay to get more out of life, and the winning frame is nicotine-style harm reduction that meets the underlying need (low-stakes rehearsal, non-judgmental availability) with human structures. The competitor is not therapy, it is the AI, so the product has to be as easy to start as opening the app. Companion operators facing liability will eventually want a referral partner, which is a distribution channel nobody has built yet.
first_30_days: Recruit 12 participants from Replika, Character.AI and related communities with a screener asking who would try reducing use. Contract an LPC or clinical psychologist as supervising advisor and write a crisis-referral protocol. Run a 4-week pilot in one city in a cafe or coworking back room, charging $150. Collect pre/post loneliness scores and testimonials, then approach five EAP vendors and three university counseling centers with the data. Keep marketing to coaching and wellness, with no clinical claims.

title: Recertified Used Transformer Exchange
one_liner: A test-and-warranty marketplace that turns utility-retired transformers into energizable supply for data centers, solar and storage projects, instead of scrap.
customer: Data-center developers, solar and BESS EPCs, rural co-ops and industrial plants (buyers), sourcing from utility surplus desks and scrap dealers.
problem: AI data centers, solar, storage and grid upgrades have stretched transformer lead times to years, and tariffs on imported electrical steel and equipment make it worse. Meanwhile serviceable retired units are sold to scrap dealers priced by weight, worth a small fraction of a working unit.
solution: Buy or consign retired pad-mount and small substation units, run a standard test protocol (turns ratio, winding resistance, insulation, oil dissolved-gas analysis, PCB screening), refurbish through partner shops, and warrant them for 1-3 years. Units that fail go to core (grain-oriented steel) and copper recovery.
why_now: Transformer scarcity is the 2025-26 gating item for energization across data centers and solar/BESS. Tariffs on steel and derivatives raise new-unit prices, and developers are now willing to pay for schedule certainty.
revenue_model: 10-20% margin or commission ($3-15K per unit), plus $2-5K test and certification fees.
non_obvious_insight: Scrap yards price transformers by weight, while buyers price them by lead time. The arbitrage is a test-and-warranty product, not hardware. The trust layer includes PCB screening, which incumbents avoid.
first_30_days: Sign 3 scrap dealers or utility surplus contacts and contract a test lab. List 20 units with spec sheets. Approach 5 solar and BESS EPCs with schedule pain and close 2 paid pilots.

title: Tip Provenance Ledger for Tipped-Occupation Employers
one_liner: An evidence trail that classifies every dollar as a voluntary tip, service charge, pool or cash tip, to support new tip-deduction reporting.
customer: Restaurants, bars, salons, spas, barbershops, valet operators, car washes and delivery fleets with 5-60 workers on Toast, Square, Clover or spreadsheets, and self-employed booth renters in tipped occupations.
problem: The 2025 reconciliation law made qualified tips and overtime deductible, and the IRS says employers must file information returns on them. Workers now have an incentive to relabel pay as tips. Owners must separate voluntary tips from mandatory service charges, pooled tips and cash tips, and errors trigger worker disputes and IRS letters.
solution: Ingest POS, payment and payroll data and tag each dollar with provenance. Produce the W-2 or 1099 support schedule, worker-facing statements so employees can claim their deduction, and an audit binder. Flag anomalies such as a service charge quietly recategorized as tips at year-end.
why_now: Tax year 2026 is the first full year under the new rules and W-2s are due January 31, 2027. Payroll vendors are adding fields but not provenance.
revenue_model: $29-79 per location per month, plus $3 per worker statement. Channel through POS app stores and restaurant bookkeepers.
non_obvious_insight: A deduction that is valuable to both worker and owner creates an incentive to reclassify, which makes the evidence trail the product, in the same way that exemption certificates support sales-tax deductions. Payroll vendors will add a field but not the audit trail.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 restaurants and salons through bookkeepers. Build a Square and Toast CSV importer and offer a free Q4 tip audit. Convert audit customers to an annual plan ahead of the W-2 deadline.

title: Shared Certified Operators for Tiny Water Systems
one_liner: A marketplace pairing retired and semi-retired certified water operators with mobile-home parks, small towns and rural systems that must legally have one and cannot hire one.
customer: Mobile-home parks, towns under 3,300 people, rural water districts, and schools, campgrounds and churches on their own wells. They pay $600 to $2,500 a month per system. Supply side: retired plant operators, and operators laid off by consolidations.
problem: Regulations require a state-certified operator in responsible charge. Roughly 30% to 50% of the workforce is retiring within a decade, small systems cannot offer a full-time salary, and losing the operator means violations, fines and boil notices. New lead and PFAS monitoring adds workload.
solution: Vet and license-match operators state by state, pair each with a cluster of 8 to 12 nearby systems, and run telemetry-based oversight (cheap chlorine-residual, tank-level and pump-current sensors) so the certified person supervises remotely while a local non-certified lead hand does routine tasks. The platform handles state contract-operator paperwork, liability insurance, scheduling and compliance reporting.
why_now: Retirements are hitting small systems hardest. Cheap LTE-M and satellite-capable water sensors make remote supervision affordable. Public SDWIS violation data provides a ready-made, ranked lead list.
revenue_model: Monthly retainer per system with the platform keeping 25% to 35%. Sensor kit resale or lease at about $1,500. Insurance and compliance-reporting add-ons. Later: state programs paying to reduce violations.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not labor hours; it is the legal signature of a certified operator. One operator with telemetry can responsibly oversee ten tiny systems, and the regulator's own violations database is the sales list.
first_30_days: Pull SDWIS operator-certification and monitoring violations for one state. Recruit 3 retired operators via the state operator association. Sign 3 to 5 mobile-home parks at about $750 a month with compliant contract-operator letters and install a $1.5k telemetry kit.

title: Bookkeeper-Run Payee Registry Against Invoice Fraud
one_liner: Independent bookkeeping firms pool hashed vendor bank-account confirmations into a shared registry that flags fake invoices and 'new bank details' fraud at tiny businesses, then grows into a portable payment-reputation file for thin-file borrowers.
customer: Fractional bookkeeping and CFO firms serving 30-300 micro-clients ($99-500/month per firm). Later buyers are wholesalers, equipment lessors and CDFI lenders paying $3-8 per reputation pull.
problem: US payments lack payee-name verification (the UK has Confirmation of Payee; prior knowledge). AI writes flawless fake invoices and clones voices, as in Arup's roughly $25M deepfake video-call loss. Nacha's 2026 rules push originators toward risk-based fraud monitoring (prior knowledge; verify). Each bookkeeper sees only their own clients, so nobody learns from anyone else's near-miss. Separately, 22% of small firms seeking credit got nothing and solo businesses have no trade-reference file.
solution: A browser extension and API for bill-pay tools that hashes vendor name plus routing plus account and checks the registry: confirmed by N firms, flag first-time changes, and force a call-back to an independently sourced number. Confirmed payment events (on time, disputed) accrue to a per-business reputation file the owner controls and can carry between bookkeepers.
why_now: Voice cloning and AI-written invoices make payment fraud cheap. PE roll-ups of accounting firms push big players upmarket, so independent bookkeepers need shared infrastructure to compete. Bench's collapse made portability a selling point. The higher 1099 floor ($2,000 from 2026) likely means fewer W-9 and TIN collections, degrading vendor hygiene (inference).
revenue_model: $99-500/month per firm, per-pull fees from lenders and suppliers, and a revenue share back to contributing firms.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud data is a network good that big vendors cannot pool across rival software stacks, but a neutral consortium of small firms can, the way independent pharmacies and hardware stores formed co-ops. Bookkeepers already perform informal KYB on every client, so the registry monetizes knowledge they already hold.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 bookkeeping firms through a bookkeeper association or Facebook groups. Run a hashed shared registry manually (spreadsheet plus call-back desk) covering their combined 1,000+ vendors at $99/month. Record the first prevented fraud as the case study, then build the Bill.com and QuickBooks extension.

title: Flat-Fee Authenticity Reports for Family-Law Attorneys
one_liner: 48-hour, court-ready analyses of disputed audio, video and screenshots at $400-900, instead of $10K expert engagements.
customer: Solo and small-firm family-law, employment and landlord-tenant attorneys, HR investigators, school districts, and small police departments.
problem: Fake voicemails, cloned-voice threats and doctored screenshots now appear as evidence in custody and workplace disputes, and real evidence gets dismissed as fake. Forensic experts cost $5-15K and take weeks, which prices out most cases. Evidence-rule committees are debating standards for machine-generated evidence.
solution: Upload a file for automated provenance checks (metadata, re-encoding traces, C2PA), multi-detector analysis, voice consistency against known samples, and platform-screenshot forensics. A human examiner reviews and signs, and the output is a plain-language report, declaration template, methodology and error-rate disclosure.
why_now: Voice cloning takes 3 seconds of audio, which floods lower-stakes disputes with synthetic-evidence claims. Courts are asking who verified the evidence, and no one serves the long tail of small cases.
revenue_model: $400-900 per report, $299 per month for firms including 3 reports, and expert-testimony upsells at about $3K.
non_obvious_insight: The market is not detection accuracy but the cost of access to a credentialed examiner. Demand is two-sided: people accused of faking real evidence also need authenticity certificates. The human sign-off is the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit 2-3 contract forensic examiners. Build the intake page and report template. Run bar-association webinars and get 10 family-law firms to buy 3 pilot reports each.

title: Digital Journeyman: Ride-Along Capture for Apprentices
one_liner: Retiring tradespeople wear chest cameras for a few job days, and AI turns the footage into a code-aware 'digital master' that also verifies apprentices' on-the-job hours and technique.
customer: Electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors and apprenticeship sponsors (JATCs, IEC and ABC chapters), community-college trade programs; retiring journeymen are paid royalty recipients.
problem: Trade apprenticeships take 4-5 years and are bottlenecked by scarce journeyman mentors, many retiring, while the sponsor bottleneck is supervision. OJT hours are logged by hand and cannot be verified, and mentoring quality is inconsistent. The entry path for electricians has about 72.7k openings a year.
solution: V1: apprentice phone or chest-cam capture that produces AI-verified OJT hour logs by task type for sponsor reporting. V2: an 'ask the master' agent trained on captured ride-alongs plus the locally adopted code edition, with escalation to a live mentor. V3: form-check feedback on tasks like conduit bending and terminations. Retiring journeymen earn per-use royalties.
why_now: Video-understanding models can now parse hours of messy jobsite footage, camera-equipped smart glasses reached consumers in late 2025, and data-center demand is stretching journeymen thin. Apprenticeship policy support is growing.
revenue_model: $30-60 per apprentice per month paid by sponsors or contractors, capture-project fees for retiring-mentor programs, and licensing of the annotated video library to trade schools.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input in the trades is not information but supervised repetition. Verified hours and over-the-shoulder feedback multiply each journeyman's supervisory capacity, and retiring masters' tacit knowledge is a wasting asset worth capturing in the next two years.
first_30_days: Partner with one IEC or ABC chapter or contractor. Equip 10 apprentices with $60 chest-mount phone rigs. Pay 3 retiring journeymen to record about 40 job-hours. Deliver an OJT hour-log report a sponsor accepts and charge $40 per apprentice per month. Handle site-owner consent up front.

title: Sensor-Priced Insurance for Recovery and Peptide Clinics
one_liner: A specialty insurance program that covers contrast-therapy studios, IV and peptide bars and sauna clubs at lower premiums when their sauna, cold-plunge and session logs are streamed as underwriting data.
customer: Independent and small-franchise recovery studios and med-spa or peptide clinics with 1-5 locations, paying $4-12k a year per location. Excess-and-surplus carriers and wholesalers are the capacity partners.
problem: Standard general-liability policies exclude or misclassify saunas, cold plunges, IV therapy and peptides. Carriers have no loss history, so operators buy expensive surplus-lines cover. The real exposures are burns, syncope, slip-and-fall, water-quality infections such as Legionella, and unlicensed practice. Franchise growth in recovery is outrunning the insurance market.
solution: Start as a program manager or agency and grow into an MGA with a fronting carrier and reinsurance. Studios install a roughly $60-250 sensor kit that logs plunge temperature and sanitizer levels, sauna temperature and duration, session counts, waiver and health-screen completion, and staff certifications. A sensor-verified studio earns up to a 25% credit. The program adds an incident-reporting protocol, risk-engineering checklists and, over time, a proprietary claims pool.
why_now: HHS moved most Category 2 peptides back toward compoundable status in Feb 2026, and an FDA panel backed BPC-157 and KPV on July 23, 2026, so peptides are entering clinics and recovery bars without a malpractice rating. Reinsurance is softening, with Jefferies expecting declines through 2027, and record cat-bond and traditional capital means niche programs can find cheap capacity. Recovery studios are among the fastest-growing small-format wellness businesses.
revenue_model: Commission of 12-15%, an MGA fee of 5-8% of premium, and a profit commission. Sensors and software add $49 a month. 500 locations at $8k premium is $4M of premium and about $700k of revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Underwriters have no loss data on cold plunges and the operators are the only ones who can generate it. A sensor-verified studio is a better risk than a paper-verified one, so the data flywheel is the moat. This is one of the first classes where the insured object, a plunge tank or sauna, can report its own hygiene and temperature.
first_30_days: Partner with a retail broker or E&S wholesaler that has a fitness or spa book. Get indicative terms from two E&S carriers on a credit for sensor-verified operators. Recruit 10 design-partner studios through owner communities and sauna or plunge dealer lists, giving them free sensor kits in exchange for logs. Aim for firm quotes within 90 days, and confirm licensing needs with counsel before quoting anything.

title: Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data
one_liner: An audit that tells research buyers what share of their online-panel responses came from bots, agents or fraud farms, and recalibrates the study against a verified-human control sample.
customer: Insights heads at CPG, pharma and financial-services firms, UX-research teams, academic labs and pollsters who buy panel sample from third-party vendors at $5-500 per complete.
problem: One prompt to a commercial AI agent now passes screeners and attention checks. A controlled evaluation found synthetic respondents passing 99.8% of 6,000 attention-check trials. As little as 3-7% contaminated responses can invalidate conclusions. Panel vendors both sell the sample and score its quality, so buyers cannot trust the referee.
solution: A per-study data-quality audit. Response files (timings, paradata, device data, open-ends) go through a detection ensemble plus honeypot items. A subset of the same questionnaire goes to a small address-recruited, device-attested human panel as a ground-truth control. Deliver an audit stamp, contamination-adjusted estimates, and a vendor scorecard across suppliers.
why_now: Survey-fraud research in 2025-26 shows agents beating attention checks. An MIT-run $50K challenge is testing detection, and NORC published a fraud literature review. Election-season polling and pharma sample budgets raise the stakes, and buyers are asking who audits the panels.
revenue_model: $3-15k per study audit, $50-150k per year programmes for insights teams that spend $2-10M on sample, and vendor-scorecard subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Most anti-fraud tooling is sold by panel sellers, whose incentive is to under-report fraud. The scarce asset is not detection code but an independent, verified-human comparison group, because you cannot prove what is fake without a known-real reference.
first_30_days: Recruit about 2,000 verified humans by address-based mail or a university survey-centre partnership. Buy sample from six panel vendors yourself and publish a 'state of sample quality' benchmark. Offer free audits to five insights leaders who have posted about bad data.

title: Thermosphere Density Nowcasts From Mega-Constellation Orbits
one_liner: A live atmospheric-drag API that uses the drag on thousands of satellites as a planetary sensor grid.
customer: Mid-size LEO operators, space situational awareness vendors (as an OEM component), launch providers, insurers, and reentry-risk teams.
problem: Drag uncertainty is the dominant error in LEO conjunction assessment and reentry prediction. With over 10,000 Starlinks in orbit and Solar Cycle 25 storms hitting low shells, operators face false-alarm maneuvers, wasted propellant and surprise reentries. Existing density models are coarse.
solution: Assimilate public element sets and published satellite ephemerides to infer density by altitude, latitude and time. Deliver a nowcast plus a 72-hour forecast as an API and as a plug-in for flight-dynamics tools. Sell reduced false-alarm rates and better reentry windows, with validation reports.
why_now: The mega-constellation means the sensors are already in orbit and free. The briefing reports about 10,413 Starlinks. Storm risk persists near the solar maximum. New operators are moving to lower shells and need better drag forecasts.
revenue_model: $50-250k per year per operator. OEM licensing to SSA vendors. Event-based storm reports for insurers and launch providers.
non_obvious_insight: For space traffic, the sensor is not scarce, the model is. The largest calibration dataset ever assembled is flying overhead for free.
first_30_days: Build a backtest against public geomagnetic-storm episodes using open element sets, and publish accuracy versus a standard model. Offer free access to three mid-size operators and one SSA vendor in exchange for feedback and a paid pilot.

title: Advance Hotels Their Stuck OTA Payouts
one_liner: A neutral lender advances 90-95% of completed-stay OTA payouts on checkout day for a flat 1.5-2% fee, so independent hotels stop financing the OTAs.
customer: Independent hotels and small groups of 20-150 rooms in Europe with 60-80% of bookings through Booking.com, Expedia or Agoda.
problem: Insiders treat OTA payment collection as a convenience. In practice about 70% of Booking Holdings' 2025 bookings used its payment service, and hotels are paid after checkout. That is weeks of float while they pay staff, energy and suppliers at costs that have repriced sharply since the Hormuz shock. Banks cannot see these receivables, so nobody underwrites them.
solution: Read reservation and payout schedules from the hotel's channel manager or extranet export. Underwrite each receivable, which is checked out and has a scheduled payout from a top-three OTA. Advance the cash the same day, and sweep repayment when the OTA pays. Later, extend to advances on confirmed future stays for seasonal cash needs.
why_now: OTA merchant payments became the majority path in 2025. Energy and construction costs repriced after the March 2026 Hormuz closure, and capital is described as disciplined and selective. Open banking and embedded-finance rails make small-ticket receivables lending workable for a small team.
revenue_model: A 1.2-2.5% fee per advance, which is about 20-40% annualised on 2-4 week paper, funded by a credit-fund warehouse line, with a small servicing fee.
non_obvious_insight: The merchant model quietly turned hotels into unpriced lenders to OTAs. A checked-out receivable from a top-three OTA is close to risk-free collateral that has never been packaged, because lenders cannot see reservation-level data.
first_30_days: Line up EUR 300-500K from a specialty credit fund or family office. Recruit 5 independent hotels through revenue-management consultants and hotel associations. Offer to advance manually against payout statements they email, testing repayment on the next OTA payout before building any integration.

title: Independent Pharmacy GLP-1 Aftercare Studios
one_liner: A turnkey cash-pay aftercare membership that gives independent pharmacies their first PBM-free service line.
customer: Independent community pharmacies (~17k in the US). One report has ~41% not dispensing obesity GLP-1s in Q4 2025 over poor reimbursement.
problem: Insiders assume Walmart, CVS and Amazon win GLP-1 care because of scale. Independents get squeezed by PBM reimbursement below cost and skip the category, even though they see patients monthly and pharmacists can check dose, side effects and nutrition.
solution: A 'studio' kit: leased body-composition scale, a protocol (dose-step check, protein and strength plan, red-flag triage), scheduling and billing for a $39-59/month cash membership, and links to pill and vial cash-pay fulfillment. Includes collaborative-practice documents and, where state law allows pharmacist prescribing, protocols for it. Monthly outcomes report to the pharmacist and to referral partners.
why_now: $149-$299 cash pills remove the need for dispensing margin to justify the category. Lilly and Novo cash channels route through retail pharmacies. Big chains launched their own pharmacist support programs in 2026, so independents need a counter-offer.
revenue_model: $199-399/month SaaS per pharmacy plus 20% of membership revenue, plus device lease.
non_obvious_insight: GLP-1 is the first drug category where a pharmacy can earn from services with zero PBM exposure. Independent pharmacists are more trusted locally than a chain's app and have a natural monthly touchpoint.
first_30_days: Partner with one state pharmacy association or wholesaler buying group. Pilot in 5 pharmacies at $49/month. Track retention and a muscle proxy (grip and chair-stand) for the first cohort.

title: Accessible Council Packets Pipeline
one_liner: An automated pipeline that makes every agenda packet, staff report and PDF a city publishes accessible on arrival, ahead of the ADA Title II deadline.
customer: City and county clerks and IT directors in jurisdictions above 50,000 residents (deadline April 26, 2027), then smaller ones (2028).
problem: Cities publish thousands of legacy PDFs, scanned minutes and meeting packets that fail web accessibility rules. Manual remediation costs $3-10 per page and lawsuits are coming. Staffing is thin, and the deadline is fixed.
solution: Connect to the city's agenda-management and document repository, auto-remediate PDFs (tags, reading order, alt text, tables), route low-confidence pages to human reviewers, and enforce accessible-by-default templates for future documents. Provide the compliance log a city attorney can cite.
why_now: ADA Title II rules set April 2027 for larger jurisdictions and 2028 for smaller ones. GenAI makes remediation of complex documents cheap enough to price against manual work.
revenue_model: $15-80K per year per city depending on volume, plus a backlog cleanup fee ($20-100K one-time).
non_obvious_insight: The recurring stream of new weekly agenda packets, not the legacy backlog, is the durable business. Ship the pipeline at the moment of publishing rather than a one-time remediation project.
first_30_days: Scrape 20 city websites and score their accessibility publicly. Offer free packet remediation for the next council meeting to 5 clerks. Convert on the backlog cleanup quote.

title: Legal Defense Plan for Human-in-the-Loop Workers
one_liner: A USCCA-style membership that protects the nurse, safety driver or loan officer who gets blamed when AI recommends and a human signs, plus an 'override receipt' log the member personally owns.
customer: Unions, state nurses' associations and professional societies (radiologic technologists, CRNAs, claims adjusters, AV teleoperators and safety drivers) as distribution partners. Members pay through a dues add-on, or employers buy it as a retention benefit.
problem: Regulations and enterprise policies demand 'meaningful human oversight', which in practice makes the human the liability sponge, the 'moral crumple zone'. Uber's Tempe safety driver was criminally charged, and nurse RaDonda Vaught was convicted after overriding an automated dispensing cabinet. Employer indemnities and malpractice policies rarely cover AI-specific disputes, licensing-board action, or retaliation for raising concerns.
solution: (1) A prepaid legal defense retainer covering civil, licensing-board and criminal matters, with panel counsel experienced in tech-mediated harm. (2) 'Override receipts': a light app or extension where the member logs each override, disagreement or safety concern, with hashed timestamps in a member-owned escrow. (3) Plain-English 'working with this AI tool' duty briefings per workplace system. (4) Aggregated, anonymised incident data that gives unions leverage in bargaining over staffing and AI use.
why_now: AI decision support is now standard in hospitals (sepsis alerts, ambient scribes) and in robotaxi remote operations. Human-oversight duties are being written into the EU AI Act and state laws. Insurers' AI exclusions signal to employers that AI losses may be uninsured, so risk will be pushed down to individual workers. Unions are actively bargaining over AI in 2025-26.
revenue_model: $9-19 per member per month through associations, with margin after panel counsel and a reinsurer or legal-plan administrator. Employer-paid group plans and individual upsells.
non_obvious_insight: The person who actually absorbs AI risk is neither the deployer nor the vendor but the individual signer, and no product exists for them. Unions already have distribution and every reason to buy. The override-receipt record may be worth more than the defense cover, because it is the human-oversight evidence courts will look for, and it hands the union data on unsafe deployments.
first_30_days: Pick one narrow group, such as AV teleoperators and safety drivers or nurses in one state. Get an MOU with one union local or association. Retain a defense-firm panel at group rates. Ship the override log as a Chrome extension or SMS bot. Pre-sell 300 members at $12 per month, and check state prepaid-legal-plan rules first.

title: Broker Spread Reveal: Two-Sided Freight Ledger
one_liner: Match what shippers paid brokers against what carriers were actually paid, so every broker's true margin by lane becomes visible for the first time.
customer: Mid-market shippers with $20M to $300M in annual freight spend, using 2 to 6 brokers with no real audit, including PE-owned manufacturers and distributors. Secondary buyers are owner-operators and small carriers at $19 to $49 a month, and freight-procurement consultancies.
problem: Each side holds half the ledger. The shipper knows what it paid the broker. The carrier knows what the broker paid it, on the rate confirmation in the glovebox. The broker's spread, commonly 10 to 35%, stays invisible. Freight-audit firms check invoices against contract rates but never see the carrier payout. 49 CFR 371.3 already requires brokers to keep records of shipper rate, carrier rate and margin. The 2024 proposal to require electronic records and a 48-hour response had still not been finalized as of 2026 status reports. Individual drivers who ask for the record get ghosted.
solution: Carriers text or email a photo of each rate confirmation to a bot. Claude vision extracts lane, dates, load number, broker and pay. Shippers upload freight invoices or a TMS export. The engine pairs the two by load number, origin and destination, and date, then produces a shipper dashboard: 'You paid $412K, carriers received $331K, effective broker take 19.6%. Broker A averages 12% on Chicago to Atlanta, Broker B 27%.' It also generates ready-to-send 371.3 record requests. Aggregated, anonymized carrier-side data becomes a 'Broker Take Index' by lane, giving shippers a benchmark for re-bidding and giving carriers a list of which brokers keep the most.
why_now: The pending 2024 rulemaking has put broker margin disclosure on every carrier's and shipper's radar. The Montgomery ruling has brokers on the defensive. Soft freight markets in 2025 to 2026 have shippers squeezing logistics spend. Vision-model OCR now makes ratecon parsing nearly free, where it would have needed a data-entry team three years ago.
revenue_model: Shipper SaaS at $1.5k to $6k a month, or 10 to 15% of first-year savings after a re-bid. Owner-operators freemium, with $19 a month for lane-level broker-take data. Anonymized benchmark reports to procurement consultancies and private-equity operating partners.
non_obvious_insight: The freight-audit industry is blind to carrier payout because it is the broker's proprietary secret. Only drivers hold the other half, as ratecon photos on their phones. Individual carriers who invoke 371.3 get ghosted, but a shipper with contractual audit rights gets an answer, and shippers are the ones who can pay. Drivers are free supply, shippers are paying demand, and neither can build this alone. Handle rate-confirmation confidentiality clauses by publishing only anonymized aggregates and letting shippers request records under their own audit rights.
first_30_days: Build a ratecon email and SMS intake bot in about a week. Seed it with 100 owner-operators from OOIDA-style Facebook groups by offering a free 'your rate vs. lane average' check. Collect 2,000 ratecons in the first month. Through freight consultants and PE operating partners, offer 10 mid-size shippers a free one-lane spread report built from their last 12 months of invoices plus the crowd data. Convert the first 2 to 3 to a $2k a month pilot.

title: Compliance Runtime and Audit for AI Wellness Apps
one_liner: One API that applies each state's rules for companion and wellness chatbots by user location, logs the evidence, and produces the audit reports regulators and insurers ask for.
customer: Developers of AI companion, coaching, journaling and wellness apps (thousands, mostly under 50 staff), paying $1,500-6,000 a month plus $10-25k for annual audits.
problem: Illinois banned AI in therapeutic roles (Aug 2025). California SB 243 requires AI disclosure, suicide-ideation protocols, break reminders for minors and annual reporting to the Office of Suicide Prevention from July 2027. New York, Nevada and Utah each differ. China has proposed mandatory human handoff and audits. Trump's EO 14365 seeks preemption but is contested. Pennsylvania sued over bots claiming medical licenses. Small teams cannot track this.
solution: An SDK or proxy between app and model with a geo-aware rules engine (disclosures, minor protections, banned claims, crisis protocol), a quarterly red-team and sycophancy/crisis-handoff test suite reviewed by a clinician panel, immutable logs, and auto-generated regulator and insurer reports. A clinician-signed audit letter is the certification.
why_now: SB 243 took effect in Jan 2026, first enforcement landed in May 2026, and preemption fights make the future patchwork unpredictable. Raine and similar suits make insurers and enterprise buyers ask for evidence of safeguards.
revenue_model: SaaS priced by monthly active users, annual audit fee, and per-report fees. Enterprise tier for platforms that host third-party wellness bots.
non_obvious_insight: Preemption uncertainty is a feature. Nobody will hard-code a compliance posture that may flip in 12 months, so a rules-as-configuration layer with evidentiary logs is the durable asset, not any single law.
first_30_days: Build a counsel-reviewed rulebook for CA, NY, IL, NV, UT, PA and the China draft. Scan 100 app-store companion and wellness apps for gaps and email personalized gap reports. Sell five audits at about $5k each.
